Narrow the absolute exclusion to all other production implementation and bind the allowed contracts.py bytes in the final manifest. blockers.finding: The contract requires checkout/.work/batch/transaction-inspect replacement during the invocation to fail closed, but stage_bytes authenticates and closes a fresh directory chain independently for each file. The contract freezes multiple calls without freezing a common directory-identity baseline or a final complete-layout postcheck. A local actor can replace the batch or transaction-inspect directory between two successful stage_bytes calls, so content may be installed in one directory epoch and bundle.json in another while the wrapper can still report success. The post-return mutation disclaimer does not cover replacement before return.
blockers.minimal_fix: Keep stage_bytes as the sole writer, but freeze an invocation-level checkout/.work/batch/transaction-inspect identity baseline once the first call establishes it; compare identities before and after every subsequent call and before returning, and verify the complete exact content-plus-bundle layout in the same final directory epoch. Map any within-invocation replacement to WORK_PATH_UNSAFE. Add deterministic batch/transport replacement tests between content calls and between last content and bundle. If the existing public primitive cannot expose enough identity evidence, explicitly authorize a narrow staging helper change in the later implementation work package rather than silently weakening the guarantee.
